tasks.name: Design: closing the sandbox's boundary gaps
tasks.description:
Settle, with the maintainer, how the sandbox closes the gaps of [the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md) S1, S2, S3, S16, S17, S18, B7 and B8, then write the decisions into [the sandbox's design](docs/running-components-in-the-sandbox.md) and [its protocol](docs/sandbox-protocol.md) before any code changes. The points are coupled: what a frame is sent depends on who it is for, and when a frame is believed depends on how it was made.

## Points to settle
- **S1, a frame that navigates itself:** the parent says hello only for a load it started; any other `load` fails the frame and shows the fallback. Whether the host page's `frame-src` becomes a stated requirement, and whether `runCheck` probes it.
- **S2, code per pack:** `ComponentCode` carries its pack (or a trust key), and a permissive frame gets only its own pack's permissive code plus strict code; another pack's permissive component there is `not-here`.
- **S3, B8, correlation:** compile, image and host requests matched by numeric id, with a timeout each; a superseded request is rejected; only a matched answer is cached.
- **S16, frame mode's `set`:** own keys only, and whether a page frame may set any document input or only bound ones.
- **S17, `link`:** checked with `safeUrl` in the parent, and the docs say its URL and timing are untrusted.
- **S18:** whether a frame refuses to start unless `self.origin === "null"`, and whether the `sandbox` header becomes a MUST.
- **B7:** trust and print keyed by a component's entry (example scope included), not its name.
- **B8:** one reload rule for page, use and compile frames; a version mismatch answered so the parent reports `version`.

## Done when
The design and the protocol doc lead with these decisions, the protocol doc's message tables match `src/protocol/messages.ts` (audit I1), and the follow-up tasks below match what was decided (update them with `atm task edit`).

tasks.name: Decide the audit's spec questions
tasks.description:
Five findings of [the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md) need the spec to say something it doesn't. Settle each with the maintainer, then change the spec (with its changelog entry under `### Unreleased` and conformance cases), or record why not.

- **A release's own name (S4, processor side):** a processor refuses a pack release whose `package.json` `name` isn't the imported pack's name (§6.4), so a release can't arrive under another pack's name.
- **A nesting limit (S9):** a maximum depth for the document tree and for expansion, with a diagnostic, so a deep document is refused instead of overflowing the stack (§8.5 says expansion always terminates).
- **W109 (S28):** §8.1 says interpolation never produces a URL's scheme, but its second sentence checks only a URL that starts with one; `[x](java{{md.input.s}})` gets no warning.
- **Work, not only nodes (S5):** whether F034's limit counts iterations and invocations as well as nodes made (§8.5).
- **Authors' classes and ids (S31):** whether `class` and `id` params stay as written on the host's page, or are prefixed or filtered (§15).

## Done when
Each point is in the spec or recorded as declined, and the processor tasks that depend on it say what was decided.

tasks.name: Sandbox: a frame that navigates itself is failed, not admitted again
tasks.description:
Audit S1 and B8 ([the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md)), as the design task decided.

Today `frameUse` says hello on every `load` (`npm-packages/sandbox/src/use.ts`), so a strict frame that runs `location.replace(...)` sends its data away in the URL, and the page that loads is then given a port, the code, the part with the document's inputs, and `host` when the use has it. The page and compile frames say hello once (`pages.ts`, `host/runtime.ts`), so a moved container leaves them hung.

## Change
- One frame-making helper (audit A3) that owns the `sandbox` and `allow` attributes, the hello, and the reload rule, used by `frameUse`, `framePage` and the compile frame.
- A `load` the parent didn't start fails the frame: removed, its fallback shown, the observer told.
- Each reload no longer leaks a channel and a `serveHost` listener in `#frameEvents`.
- `runCheck` probes the page's `frame-src`, if the design says so.

## Tests
Browser tests in Chrome and WebKit: a strict frame that navigates itself (with `location`, and with a link clicked after `stopPropagation`) shows its fallback and gets no second hello; a page frame whose container moves recovers or fails as the design says.

tasks.name: Sandbox: a permissive frame gets only its own pack's code
tasks.description:
Audit S2 and B7 ([the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md)), as the design task decided.

`HostRuntime.#frame` gives a frame `codeFor(this.#code, level)`, every component at or below its level, and the frame imports all of it (`npm-packages/sandbox/src/frame/runtime.ts`). So a document using permissive packs A and B runs B's code in A's frame, with A's network and `host`, against spec §15. Trust and print are also keyed by name only (`host/runtime.ts` `set`), so a document's `chart` and an example's `chart` overwrite each other.

## Change
- `ComponentCode` carries its pack (or the design's trust key).
- A permissive frame is sent its own pack's permissive code and the strict code; another pack's permissive component there renders as `not-here`.
- Trust and print are keyed by the component's entry (`entryOf`).

## Tests
Two permissive packs with different `network`, used in one document: each frame loads only its own pack's module (a module's top level that records where it ran), and B's use in A's slot gets its own frame. A document `chart` and an example `chart` of different trust each keep theirs.

tasks.name: Sandbox: requests matched to their answers by id, with a timeout
tasks.description:
Audit S3, B8 and R7, through the helper A2 ([the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md)).

`connectCompiler` keeps pending requests by component name (`npm-packages/sandbox/src/protocol/compiler.ts`): a second request with the same name replaces the first, the first answer resolves the second, the first never settles, and `compiledWith` caches the wrong code under the second source's key. Image requests are matched by URL (`frame-end.ts`), host calls by id (`host-api.ts`). The compile frame has no timeout after `ready`.

## Change
One small `request`/`answer` helper with numeric ids, a `Map`, and a timeout per request; used for compile, image and host calls. A superseded request is rejected; only an answer matched to its own request is cached. Drop the doc comment that says an older request "never settles".

## Tests
Two compiles of the same name with different sources each get their own code, and Cache Storage holds each under its own key; a document and an example defining the same name both render; a compile that never answers rejects after the timeout and its use shows its fallback.

tasks.name: Sandbox: every message from a frame checked by one table
tasks.description:
Audit S16, S17, the shape checks of S28, and A1 ([the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md)), as the design task decided.

## Change
- One table per direction, `type → guard`, shared by both ends, from which `TO_FRAME`/`FROM_FRAME`, the TypeScript unions and `isMessage` derive; `isMessage` narrows only after the shape passes. Test `protocol.schema.json` against it.
- `set` in frame mode: `typeof input === "string" && Object.hasOwn(inputs, input)` (today `input in inputs`, `npm-packages/sandbox/src/pages.ts`), and bound inputs only if the design says so.
- `link`: a string, through `safeUrl(url, schemes)` in the parent (`protocol/parent-end.ts`); `ViewEvents.link`'s doc says the URL and its timing come from the frame.
- `pong`: an integer with `answered < n <= sent`.
- `error`, `rendered`, `size` and `serveHost`'s `data` checked before use; a reported frame height capped.

## Tests
From a fake frame's port: `set` of `__proto__` is refused; `link` with `javascript:` is dropped; `pong {n: Infinity}` doesn't stop a hung frame being reported; a malformed `error` reaches no host callback.

tasks.name: Sandbox: the image gate decides on the image's resolved origin
tasks.description:
Audit S15 and the `allow-origin` point of S28 ([the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md)).

`ImageGate.decide` takes `//tracker.example/p.png` as relative (`urlScheme` gives `undefined`, `npm-packages/sandbox/src/image-gate.ts`), so it shows without the reader being asked, and the frame fetches `new URL(src, base)`. `PageImages.allowOrigin` has the same gap. A frame's `allow-origin` also forgets the reader's stored answer before asking again.

## Change
One function decides an image's origin from `new URL(src, base)` and compares it with the base's; `decide`, `allowOrigin` and the fetch all use it. A frame's `allow-origin` asks without forgetting a stored answer, or is rate-limited per origin (the reader's own button still forgets).

## Tests
`//host/x.png`, `\\host/x.png` and `/\host/x.png` on another origin are asked about; a same-origin relative image isn't; a frame repeating `allow-origin` doesn't erase a stored deny.

tasks.name: Sandbox: the frame runtime starts only in a sandboxed frame
tasks.description:
Audit S18 ([the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md)), as the design task decided.

The frame runtime believes its parent (`npm-packages/sandbox/src/frame/runtime.ts`, the hello listener). Served without `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox allow-scripts`, any site can embed `strict.html` without a `sandbox` attribute and run code in the origin that serves it. GitHub Pages ignores `_headers`, so the project's own site serves the frames that way.

## Change
The runtime refuses to start unless `self.origin === "null"`, and says why in the console; the sandbox README makes the header a MUST if the design says so. Record what the website does about it (a second origin, or a host that honours `_headers`) as a follow-up task if it isn't settled here.

## Tests
A frame document loaded in an iframe without `sandbox` doesn't answer hello; the existing frames still start.

tasks.name: Registry: a pinned import gets only its own pack's cached release
tasks.description:
Audit S4 and I6 ([the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md)).

For a pinned import the resolver takes cached files by integrity alone (`npm-packages/registry/src/resolve.ts`, `#resolveFrom`), and the cache is keyed by integrity only (`cache.ts`). So a document can pin `@trusted/charts@1.0.0` to the integrity of an `@evil/pack` release another document cached, and get its files as `@trusted/charts`, with that pack's trust and without the deny, size and registry checks. The processor's side (a release's own name) is a spec question in the spec decisions task.

## Change
Cache entries are keyed, or tagged, by `pack@version` as well as integrity, and a hit is used only for the same pack and version; the cached path applies `denied` and `#refusal` as the fetched one does.

## Tests
Two packs: one cached; a pinned import of the other with the first's integrity is not given its files; a pinned import of the same pack and version still uses the cache.

tasks.name: Registry: a tarball's intake bounded from fetch to files
tasks.description:
Audit S10, S11, S12 and A9 ([the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md)).

- `untar` loops forever on a negative octal size (`npm-packages/registry/src/tar.ts`): an entry of size `-1024` moves the offset back.
- Only the registry's declared `unpackedSize` is checked; the download (`registry.ts` `tarball`) and the gunzip are read whole.
- A tarball URL from the metadata is fetched on any origin with the registry's headers (`registry.ts`, `proxy.ts`): a token can go to another host, and a server-side proxy fetches any address.

## Change
One bounded pipeline: fetch with a byte cap, hash, gunzip with a cap, untar with sizes that are non-negative integers and an offset that always advances. Tarballs only from the registry's origin (or headers only there), and `https:`.

## Tests
A tar with a negative size, one whose gzip expands past `maxPackSize`, one larger than declared, and metadata naming a tarball on another origin are each refused with a message; a normal pack still resolves.

tasks.name: Processor: expansion counts work, not only nodes made
tasks.description:
Audit S5, S8, the slot point of B8's list, R2 and A7 ([the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md)), within what the spec decisions task settled for §8.5.

Only `Expander::made` counts against the limit (`crates/processor/src/expand.rs`), so `each` loops and `display=contents` invocations that make no node never stop: five nested `each` over 100 items run 10^10 times. Each example has its own limit (`processor/examples.rs`), so N examples give N times the limit. Slot placement loops a template without `expanding` (`expand/text.rs`).

## Change
One `iterate` helper for `each`, `rendered_slot` and `slot` that charges each iteration, and a charge per invocation in `expanding`, reported as F034 where the spec says. Examples get what remains of the document's limit and count against it.

## Tests
Nested empty `each` loops and a doubling chain of `display=contents` definitions end with F034 quickly; many examples together hit the limit; existing F034 cases still pass; a conformance case if the spec changed.

tasks.name: Processor: CEL charges a value's cost before building it
tasks.description:
Audit S6, the `in`/`==` point of S28, and A7 ([the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md)).

The evaluator spends for a built string or list only after the call returns (`crates/processor/src/cel/eval.rs`, `built`), so `'a…'.replace('a', 'a…')` with 40,000-character strings allocates 1.6 GB before the budget error. A string literal costs one step whatever its length; `in` and deep `==` cost one step whatever the size.

## Change
An overload can say its result's size from its arguments (`replace`, `join`, `split`, `+`, `md.list`), and the evaluator spends that before calling; literals are charged by length; `contains` and `equals` by elements visited.

## Tests
The large `replace`, `split('').join(x)` and a quadratic `filter(r, r in rows)` each end with the budget error without a large allocation; the differential tests still agree.

tasks.name: Processor: the name suggestion bounded
tasks.description:
Audit S7 ([the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md)). `distance` builds a full `|a| × |b|` matrix (`crates/processor/src/nearest.rs`), and names have no length limit, so two 50,000-character names ask for about 20 GB; the "close enough" filter runs after the distance.

## Change
Skip a candidate whose length differs by more than a third before computing; compare at most a fixed length (64, say); keep two or three rows instead of the matrix.

## Tests
The existing cases; a long unknown name against long known names returns quickly; a length-mismatched candidate is never measured.

tasks.name: Processor: what the spec decisions settled
tasks.description:
Build what the spec decisions task put into the spec ([the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md) S4 processor side, S9, S28 W109, S31); leave out what it declined.

- **A release's own name:** refuse a release whose `package.json` `name` isn't the imported name, where `crates/processor/src/resolve/load/packs.rs` checks `export.pack` today.
- **A nesting limit:** refuse a tree deeper than the spec's limit in `Converter::blocks` (`parse/blocks.rs`), and carry a depth in `Expander::expanding`, with the spec's diagnostic.
- **W109:** warn whenever an interpolated value lands before a URL's first `:` (`expand/text.rs` `checked_url`).
- **Classes and ids:** as decided.

## Tests
Conformance cases for each new rule; unit tests for 10,000 nested `> ` markers and for `[x](java{{md.input.s}})`.

tasks.name: Processor: root-folder paths are checked as pack paths are
tasks.description:
Audit S21, R4 and A5 ([the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md)).

`Origin::File` holds a string joined by `joined` (`crates/processor/src/resolve/origin.rs`), which accepts any segment; `FilePath` (`crates/pack-types/src/file_path.rs`) refuses `\`, `:` and NUL. So `./..\..\secrets.csv` reaches `host::Files::file` as written, and a Windows host that joins it to a folder leaves the root.

## Change
`Origin::File` holds a `FilePath` (or a sibling newtype in `compmd-pack`); `Origin::join` is one call for both variants; `joined` is deleted. An import or data path that isn't a valid path gets the diagnostic an unreadable one gets today.

## Tests
Imports and data `from`s with `\`, `:` and NUL segments are refused before `Files` is asked; existing relative imports still resolve; coverage stays at 99%.

tasks.name: Processor: one line index per document
tasks.description:
Audit B4, B6, R1 and A8 ([the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md)).

Line starts are computed five ways: `parse/source.rs` (CR, CRLF and LF), `lines.rs` (LF only), `parse/frontmatter.rs`, `parse/edit.rs` and `load/format.rs`. In a document with CR-only line endings, `Lines` lookups by `Point.line` miss, so diagnostics for names, paths and values point at the wrong place. The CSV reader counts each record's line from the start of the file.

## Change
One `LineIndex` (line starts in bytes and code points, CR-aware) owned by the document, used by all five; the CSV reader keeps a running cursor.

## Tests
A CR-only document's diagnostics point where an LF one's do; a 100,000-row CSV's line numbers are right and it loads in linear time.

tasks.name: Processor: a data source parsed once, and a pack file read from the document's own import
tasks.description:
Audit B3, I6 and A6 ([the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md)).

- A data `from: @scope/pack/file` resolves against the first loaded document of that pack anywhere in the resolve (`crates/processor/src/load/from.rs`), so a document that doesn't import the pack can read its files, and with two versions loaded the load order decides.
- A data `from` is classified three times with different rules (`validate/data.rs` twice, `load/from.rs`).

## Change
A `DataSource` enum (file, pack, remote, host) made once from `DataImport.from`; validation checks it and loading only fills it in. A pack source records the importing document's own `ReleaseId` at resolve time.

## Tests
A document reading `@acme/kit/icons.json` without importing `@acme/kit` gets the diagnostic for an unknown pack; with two versions loaded, each document reads its own; existing data cases pass.

tasks.name: Processor: examples share the document's parse cache
tasks.description:
Audit B5 ([the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md)). Each rendering example runs with `resolve::Parses::default()` (`crates/processor/src/processor/examples.rs`), so it parses `@compmd/core`, the ambient packs and every import again, and `with_examples` (`processor/edit.rs`) rebuilds every example on every edit, also a block-only edit elsewhere.

## Change
The example processors share the processed document's `Parses`; an edit rebuilds only the examples whose block it touched (or all, when it touched imports or frontmatter).

## Tests
A document with several examples parses core once (a counting `Files`); an edit to a paragraph rebuilds no example; an edit inside one rebuilds that one. A bench in `benches/` if one fits.

tasks.name: Processor: small parser fixes from the audit
tasks.description:
The small processor findings of [the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md).

- A bare `number` param accepts what `f64::from_str` does: `inf`, `nan`, `1e999` (`crates/processor/src/cel/value.rs`). Check first whether validation refuses them; if not, one number grammar shared with `parse/yaml.rs`, and F009 for the rest (spec §5).
- CEL escapes accept a sign: `'\x+1'` (`cel/lexer.rs`); require hex digits first.
- The inline component's fallback slice can panic if the fork and `matching_bracket` disagree (`parse/inlines.rs`, `parse/line.rs`); use `get` and `checked_sub`.
- Frontmatter YAML keeps one pointer string per value, quadratic in nesting (`parse/yaml.rs`); refuse nesting past a small depth if the spec decisions task settled a limit.
- "Push once" on a `Vec` in seven places (audit R6); `IndexSet`.

## Tests
One unit test per fix.

tasks.name: Render: names from a document looked up as own keys only
tasks.description:
Audit S13, S27 and the lookup part of A4 ([the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md)).

`"constructor" in ALLOWED` is true (`npm-packages/render/src/html.ts`), so `<constructor x>` passes the raw-HTML allowlist and `allowed.includes` throws on every render. The same shape: `surface.code[node.lang]` (a fence with language `constructor` renders an empty box), `node.name in INPUTS`, `surface.components`, `surface.examples`, the frame protocol's `listeners[message.type]` (`frame.ts`), the wireframe pack's `PARTS`, `DRAW` and attributes, and the blog highlighter's `language in bundledLanguages`.

## Change
`Map`s, or one small own-key `lookup(table, name)` helper, for every table keyed by a document's or a frame's name; a `typeof data === "object"` guard in both port listeners.

## Tests
`<constructor x>` and `<toString>` render as text; fences in `constructor` and `__proto__` show their code; a frame message of type `constructor` is ignored; the wireframe part `constructor` is an error message.

tasks.name: Render: raw HTML tokenized in linear time
tasks.description:
Audit S14 ([the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md)). The `TAG` regex in `npm-packages/render/src/html.ts` lets an attribute name hold `<`, and an unclosed `<!--` scans to the end from every start, so a large `html` node (`<details <a <a …` with no `>`, or an unclosed comment) costs quadratic time; `tokensOf` runs several times per render.

## Change
A hand-written linear scanner for tags and comments, with the same allowlist and attribute rules; tokens cached per `html` node.

## Tests
The existing raw-HTML tests; 100 KB of the two inputs above tokenize in linear time (a time bound generous enough for CI, or a step count).

tasks.name: Render: an element's tag follows its rendering
tasks.description:
Audit B2 and A4 ([the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md)). `ElementView` makes its element once (`npm-packages/render/src/markdown-views.ts`), but `renderingOf` can give the same shape another tag later: `[docs][d]` renders as `<span>`, and after `[d]: https://…` is typed the update gives `<span href="…">`, not a link. The same for image references and a `wikiLink` whose answer arrives later.

## Change
The rendered tag is part of the node's shape (as `componentPending` does with `pendingTag`), so a changed tag makes a new view; or `update` replaces its element when the tag changes. Prefer whichever lets `shapeOf`, `createView` and `renderingOf` stop disagreeing.

## Tests
In the page tests: a reference link becomes a link when its definition is added, and text again when it's removed; an image reference becomes an image; a wiki link whose answer changes.

tasks.name: Render: smaller fixes from the audit
tasks.description:
The smaller renderer findings of [the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md).

- **B10:** a highlighter promise that never settles stops highlighting for the document (`npm-packages/render/src/highlight-queue.ts`); race each job with a timeout and move on.
- **B11:** a component's later fallback renders with its first render's `pass` (`component-views.ts`); keep the latest. Footnote ids `compmd-fn-N` collide between a page and its examples (`blocks.ts`); scope them per `Blocks`.
- **S5 hardening:** `safe` in `styles.ts` lets through `url(`, `/*`, quotes and unbalanced parentheses; reject them in the renderer too.
- **R4:** the `render=both` box and the plain code node built in one place (`component-views.ts`, `example-view.ts`).

## Tests
One test per fix.

tasks.name: Processor package: an open document moves only its nodes' origins
tasks.description:
Audit B1 ([the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md)). After an edit, `move` in `npm-packages/wasm/src/open-document.ts` walks every object of the nodes after the splice, params' and instances' JSON values included. A value with a key named `origin` (flight records, `{"origin": "SFO"}`) throws, and the WebAssembly document has already taken the edit, so every later splice is applied to a stale tree. Data can be remote.

## Change
Move only the `origin` of nodes, walking `children`, `slots`, `instances[].children`, `fallback` and `document` as `@compmd/render`'s `contentOf` does; never `value`.

## Tests
An open document whose data has records with an `origin` key, edited above the node that shows them, stays in step with a fresh `process` of the same text.

tasks.name: Developer Tools: workers ended, their errors heard
tasks.description:
Audit B9, R8, A2's devtools part and the devtools points of S29 and the smaller list ([the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md)).

- `mountDevtools().destroy()` leaves the editor worker and the views worker running (`npm-packages/devtools/src/Devtools.svelte`, `Panes.svelte`).
- Neither worker client listens for `error`, so a dead worker leaves "Processing…" for good (`views.ts`, `session.ts`).
- A pack whose fetch failed is never asked for again (`processing.ts`, `#asked`).
- The console drawer's drag leaks listeners on `pointercancel` (`Panes.svelte`).
- Any link with `:~:text=` is taken as a passage of the open document (`Devtools.svelte`).
- The plain view loads remote images without asking; give its page a CSP (`views.ts` `plainPage`).

## Change
One serial worker client for both, with termination and error handling; the fixes above.

## Tests
One test per fix, in the existing devtools tests.

tasks.name: Host: processing in Rust uses the bundle's policy and ambient packs
tasks.description:
Audit S19 and A3 ([the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md)). The bundle's manifest carries `policy` and `ambient` (`crates/host/src/manifest.rs`), but nothing gives them to the processor: the Tauri plugin's example, its README and `docs/tauri-plugin.md` call `resolve((), packs, &Ambient::default())`, the default policy. So `deny`, `imports: "listed"` and `refused` are not enforced when an app processes in Rust, while the page's path does apply them (`docs/hosting.md` decision 7).

## Change
Under the `processor` feature, `HostPacks` (or `Bundle`) gives a typed `Policy` and `Ambient` from the manifest; the example, the README and the design use `resolve_with` with them.

## Tests
A bundle whose config denies a pack: processing in Rust gives the same F026 the page's path gives; an ambient pack's component resolves without an import.

tasks.name: Host: a stored release written whole, and kept only once verified
tasks.description:
Audit S20 and A9's host part ([the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md)).

- Nothing in Rust checks an integrity, and `HostPacks` reports stored releases as intact; `FolderStore::keep`'s contract ("its files already checked") is a comment (`crates/host/src/folder_store.rs`).
- `keep` removes the folder, then writes file by file, then `release.json`; a failure halfway leaves files that `file()` still serves, with an immutable cache header.

## Change
`keep` takes a `VerifiedRelease` that only the tarball checker builds (the sha512 check where `docs/hosting.md` H1 plans it; a hashing crate is a new dependency, so check it against `deny.toml`). It writes into a sibling folder and renames it into place; `file()` serves only a release with `release.json`.

## Tests
A keep that fails halfway leaves the old release served, or none; a folder without `release.json` serves nothing; a release whose files don't match isn't kept.

tasks.name: Host: Rust and JavaScript serve a bundle the same way
tasks.description:
The host findings B12, B13, I2, R1, R3 and S4-host of [the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md).

- Request paths are never percent-decoded, so `dist/my chart.js` is a 404 in both `crates/host/src/respond.rs` and `npm-packages/host-js/src/respond.ts`; decode each segment in `route` before it becomes a `FilePath`, so decoded `..` is still refused.
- `folderBundle` (`npm-packages/host-js/src/node.ts`) checks neither `format` nor the hash's shape; read the manifest through the WebAssembly binding's `Manifest::parse`.
- `respond` (JS) caches a failed WebAssembly load for good; clear it on failure.
- `embedded()` drops why a bundle is unusable (`crates/tauri/src/lib.rs`); panic with the error, as `init`'s other build mistakes do.
- The plugin's no-bundle refusal lacks the contract's headers; one shared refusal in `compmd-host`.
- "Bundle first, then the store" is written three times; one `pack_file`.
- `Files` is public and reads an unchecked path; `pub(crate)`.
- `Place` has two shapes in JS; one, the processor's.

## Tests
Cases in `crates/host/fixtures/respond/cases.json` for encoded names and encoded `..`, which both implementations run.

tasks.name: Vite: a pack's files confined to the pack, read by one module
tasks.description:
Audit S21 (Vite part), S22, I4, I5, R8, B19 and A10 ([the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md)).

- A pack document's `from` with backslashes passes the `../` test and leaves the pack on Windows (`npm-packages/vite/src/packs.ts`).
- A pack's `files` globs and `name` aren't confined when a bundle is written; a folder pack without `files` publishes its whole folder (`bundle.ts`); an installed package's own `name` isn't checked against its dependency name.
- Three name patterns for a scoped pack (`registry.ts`, `vite/src/config.ts` twice); deny ranges read two ways.
- Reading a pack folder is written twice with two models (`vite/src/packs.ts`, `pack/src/pack.ts`), and the publish check reads `files` entries as literal paths (`pack/src/check.ts`).

## Change
One pack-folder module (in `@compmd/vite`, used by `@compmd/pack`): manifest and name pattern, document path, frontmatter, relative imports, confinement (no `\`, no absolute or drive prefix, resolved path inside the pack), and the published files with globs. A folder pack without `files` publishes what its documents reach. Deny ranges read as the processor reads them.

## Tests
A `from` with backslashes is refused; a glob of `../**` publishes nothing outside; an installed package whose manifest names another pack is refused; the publish check accepts `dist/*.js`.

tasks.name: Pack and Vite: rebuilds queued, and their errors logged
tasks.description:
Audit B14 and B20 ([the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md)).

- `compmd-pack dev` rebuilds every module at once on each save, with `void build(...)`: the first syntax error ends the process, and overlapping builds write the same `dist/` files and `package.json` (`npm-packages/pack/src/dev.ts`).
- The Vite plugin's watcher calls `load()` with no serialization, and `writePacks` starts with `rm`, so two quick saves interleave (`npm-packages/vite/src/plugin.ts`); it handles `change` but not `add` or `unlink`.

## Change
One serialized, debounced rebuild that logs failures; the plugin chains loads and runs only the latest; `add` and `unlink` handled.

## Tests
A save with a syntax error logs it and the next good save rebuilds; two quick saves give one consistent bundle.

tasks.name: Blog and registry proxy: servers that survive bad requests, and a build that deletes only its output
tasks.description:
Audit S23, S24, S29 (blog parts), R9, R10 and A11 ([the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md)).

- `GET /blog/%zz` throws in `fileFor`'s `decodeURIComponent` inside a `.then` success callback, an unhandled rejection that ends `cblo dev`; `GET //` throws in the listener (`npm-packages/blog/src/serve.ts`). The registry's `toNodeListener` does the same on `Host: [` or `TRACE`, and on a stream error (`npm-packages/registry/src/node.ts`).
- `cblo build --out .` deletes the blog after building it (`writeSite`); `out` resolves against the working directory.
- `cblo build` publishes a draft's assets and dot files (`build.ts`); the dev server answers any `Host`, and sends no `nosniff`.
- Giscus values and the page's CSS go into `<script>` and `<style>` without end-tag escaping (`pages.ts`, `build.ts`).

## Change
One Node static responder for an in-memory or folder site (MIME table, `nosniff`, Host check, safe decoding, 400 on bad input), used by the blog and the website's `build/static.ts`; one folder walker that skips dot files. `out` resolved against the blog and refused when it is the blog, holds it, or is inside `posts/`. The same `<` escape as `liveOf` in both inline places.

## Tests
Each bad request gets a 400 and the server keeps serving; `--out .` and `--out posts` are refused; a draft's folder isn't written.

tasks.name: Blog: a build that names what's wrong, and outputs that don't collide
tasks.description:
The blog's bugs in [the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md): B15, B16, B17, B18, I3 and the small ones.

- The dev client cache keeps a failed build and never follows a changed config or pack (`npm-packages/blog/src/build.ts`).
- Output paths collide silently: tags `C` and `C++`, a tag that slugs to `""`, a post named `tags`, an asset named `feed.xml` (`pages.ts`, `build.ts`, `slug.ts`); post file names aren't validated.
- `2026-13-45` or an invalid `lang` crash the build with a stack, not a `BlogError` naming the post (`posts.ts`).
- Feed content has URLs rebased for the post's page, not the feed (`feeds.ts`); every file under `posts/` is read as UTF-8, and a live post inlines its folder.
- The blog finds its configuration differently from the Vite plugin (`live.ts` against `vite/src/app.ts`).
- Dates in UTC in `cblo new` and `create-blog`; `npm create @compmd/blog .` writes `"name": "."`; `--port abc`; `/blog` without the slash.

## Change
A collision-checked output map that throws a `BlogError` naming both owners; the rest as listed.

## Tests

tasks.description:

- Any argument other than exactly `--dry-run` publishes for real; reject unknown arguments with a usage message.
- Any crates.io API failure counts as "not published" (`curl -sf`); skip on 200, publish on 404, stop on anything else.
- The dry run lists files and builds nothing; package the workspace crates without `--list`, and have the Tauri check package `tauri-plugin-compmd` where WebKitGTK is installed.

## Tests

tasks.name: Release: npm is staged by a job that only stages
tasks.description:
Audit S25, the npm part of B25, R12 and I7 ([the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md)). A change to the release workflows, made with the maintainer.

- The release job holds `id-token: write` while it installs and runs every dependency's build scripts and tests (`.github/workflows/release.yml`); split it into a build-check-pack job without the token that uploads the tarballs, and a small job with it that only downloads them and stages; no caches on the staging path. The same for the two pack release workflows.
- "Already on npm" is decided by `npm view`'s exit status; compare its output with the version.
- The package list of a release is written six times; derive it once.
- `release-mermaid.yml` and `release-wireframe.yml` are the same 50 lines; one reusable workflow with a pack input, using `./.github/actions/webkit`.

## Done when
A release's dry run on a test tag (or `workflow_dispatch`) stages nothing it shouldn't, and RELEASING.md says how the jobs are split.

tasks.name: CI: the site checked before merge, and deployed for what it ships
tasks.description:
Audit B21, B22, B23 and I8 ([the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md)). Workflow changes, made with the maintainer.

- The Pages path filter omits `npm-packages/sandbox`, `devtools`, `vite`, `registry`, `crates/pack-types`, `spec/compmd-registry-v1.md` and `conformance/`; the Tauri filter omits `wasm`, `host-js`, `pack`, the fork, `Cargo.lock` and the toolchain.

- The first released spec tag will probably meet the `github-pages` environment's branch rule, and a tag run builds the whole site from the tag's commit; decide the rule and whether a tag run builds from `main`.
- Three documents say the site deploys on a release tag; it deploys on `spec-v*` only, so the install line can name a version before it is installable. Decide which is meant and make the docs say it.

## Done when
A pull request touching the sandbox runs the site check; docs/releases.md, website/docs/design.md and the workflow agree.

tasks.name: Build checks: deny for the Tauri plugin, locked builds, licences in crates, tools type-checked
tasks.description:

## Done when

tasks.name: spec-revision: a cut that is whole or not at all
tasks.description:
Audit B26 ([the audit](docs/codebase-audit.md)). `cut` writes the spec, the companion and the changelog, then commits, then tags (`tools/spec-revision/spec-revision.ts`): a failed commit leaves the files rewritten (the next cut then finds nothing under Unreleased), and an existing tag leaves the commit untagged.

## Change
Check the tag before writing; restore the files when the commit fails. Also: say when the current revision's tag is missing instead of treating the companion as unchanged; the date from the local day, not UTC; CRLF in `unreleasedOf`; and a way (or RELEASING.md's step) to write a release's header for `spec-v1.0`.

## Tests

tasks.name: Every origin for a host's own documents, and the blog's share image
tasks.description:
A static site or a blog publishes its own documents, so asking its readers about each image's or data's origin protects no one, and the question gets in the way (the first post's book club opened it over the page, and the site check couldn't click a cover). Spec §15 already lets a host configure origins; this lets a host allow every origin, and the tools use it.

## Spec (§8.6, §15)
A host MAY allow every origin instead of naming them: no origin of a document's data or images is then disallowed (F028) or asked about. It fits documents the host publishes itself; a host that shows documents others write SHOULD NOT. URL schemes, a data `from`'s literal scheme and host, credentials and sandboxes' network are unchanged. Changelog entry under Unreleased; a conformance case where `allowedOrigins: "any"` loads remote data without F028.

## Code
- **Processor:** `allowedOrigins` is a list of origins or `"any"`, in the Rust API, the WebAssembly request and its TypeScript types; the conformance README says so.
- **`@compmd/sandbox`:** the image gate takes `"any"`.
- **`@compmd/vite`:** `compmd.config.json` takes `"origins"`, `"any"` or a list of `https` origins, given to the processor's request and to the sandbox.
- **`@compmd/blog`:**
  - its own origin is always allowed;
  - the build-time render shows only images from allowed origins, any other its alt text with the button, so the built page loads no image the live one would ask about;
  - a share image (`image: {url, alt}`) in `blog.config.json` for every page, a post's own in its frontmatter, written as `og:image`, its alt and a large card.
- **The website:** the blog's share image is the site's card (`og.png`), not in a post's text; `website/blog` allows every origin.
- **The first post:** the review's corrections (links, capitalisation, wording, `updated`).

## Tests
The processor and the conformance case; the gate with `any`; the Vite config; the blog's share image, own origin, and a remote image refused at build time; `cargo make site`.

The spec doesn't change; a processor without the pack shows their fallbacks.
